author: sanjayr1
title: Quote the data-matching skill description so strict YAML parsers load it
body:
## What changed

One line in `.claude/skills/data-matching/SKILL.md`: the frontmatter `description` value is now double-quoted. The text itself is unchanged.

## Why

The description contains an unquoted `: ` ("Routes by which ID you have: email ..."). Claude Code's skill loader accepts it, but strict YAML parsers read the colon as the start of a nested mapping and reject the whole frontmatter. pi, the harness behind the gp-pi container the data team is trialing, uses such a parser and drops the skill at startup with a "Skill conflicts" warning. In the gp-pi parity audit on 2026-10-06 it was the only repo skill missing from pi's skill list.

## Verification

- pi's YAML parser (the `yaml` package in the gp-pi container) on the frontmatter. Before: `Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 3, column 14`. After: parses, `name = data-matching`, description 547 characters.
- pi 1.0.4 started with only this skill (`--no-skills --skill <fixed copy> --tools read`): the system prompt's skill list now includes `data-matching`.
- `pre-commit run --files .claude/skills/data-matching/SKILL.md`: every applicable hook passes.
- No behavior change for Claude Code: a quoted YAML string carries the same text.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only YAML frontmatter fix with no runtime or data logic changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Wraps the `data-matching` skill frontmatter **`description`** in double quotes in `.claude/skills/data-matching/SKILL.md`. The description text is unchanged; only YAML quoting changes.
> 
> Unquoted colons in the string (e.g. after “Routes by which ID you have”) break **strict YAML parsers**, which caused gp-pi to drop the skill at startup. Quoted scalars parse correctly so pi and similar loaders can register the skill like Claude Code already did.
>
